correctness.rationale: The group commutator reduces exactly to a sum of 2h signed products. Fourier inversion on the finite additive group of R requires no generating ring character. For each additive character the annihilator ideal sizes are exactly |R|, |m|, |m|/q with multiplicities 1,q−1,|R|−q; the nontrivial m-restriction is an F_q-linear functional hyperplane, valid in equal and mixed characteristics. Orthogonality yields all three formulas; their weighted sum equals |R|^(4h); the smallest is positive and the levels are distinct. The two free center coordinates multiply all horizontal fibers by |R|^2. The saturation law follows by conditioning on all horizontal coordinates lying in m. Independent explicit arithmetic checks exhaustively count rank-one horizontal fibers in seven finite rings and verify ranks two/three by exact convolution. The checker and actual output are embedded.

originality.rationale: The key exact antecedent Choosuwan–Jitman–Udomkavanich, arXiv:1605.06826v1, Theorems 3.8, 3.11 and 4.1, counts determinants over chain and finite principal ideal rings; its Section 5 explicitly calls out general finite local rings. Nonprincipal square-zero rings with d>=2 satisfy neither principal hypothesis. Prasad–Singla–Spallone, arXiv:1212.6157v2 Section 10 and Corollary 10.4, cover the same coefficient rings but classify similarity classes of individual matrices, not prescribed determinant or group commutator fibers. The closest published Heisenberg-graph and chain-ring Fourier records were read in full; they neither cover the coefficient rings nor imply all nonzero output fibers and the rank/dimension limit. Distinct output-stratum equations and comparisons checked; no exact published dominating implication found, with residual historical-character-sum risk.
residual_risks: A broad historical Fourier-character formula for fixed alternating bilinear-map fibers over arbitrary finite local rings could imply these formulas without the same terms.
Published coverage and indexed published-finding corpus search are bounded; absence of an exact search match is not proof of global uniqueness.
The proof is same-model reviewed and finite checks are independent implementations, but no independent researcher has validated the universal argument.

value.rationale: Exact prescribed-commutator fibers refine the natural commuting probability for an infinite family of non-Frobenius finite Heisenberg groups. Three distinct output strata distinguish identity, nonzero radical and unit targets and yield a universal invariant independent of the coefficient ring presentation. The conditional commuting concentration at fixed residue field and symplectic rank as radical dimension grows gives a structural limiting law. The 2016 principal-ring determinant paper explicitly raises extension of determinant counting to general local rings; the present nonprincipal square-zero case addresses a natural part of this gap without claiming the full general problem.
